body: EOSat-1 is a small Earth observation satellite in a 600 km sun-synchronous orbit, designed for a 5-year mission.
System-level requirements of the EOSat-1 mission.
The satellite launch mass, computed as the total dry mass of all units plus a 20% system margin, shall not exceed 150 kg.
The payload (optical camera and mass memory) shall consume less than 70 W in imaging mode.
The AOCS shall provide an attitude knowledge accuracy better than 10 arcsec, using at least two star trackers for redundancy.
The AOCS shall include at least four reaction wheels so that the mission survives the failure of one wheel.
The X-band downlink shall provide a data rate of at least 150 Mbps.
The battery shall provide at least 300 Wh to power the satellite during the longest eclipse.
Catalogue of the units used on EOSat-1, with their budgets.
Top-level system definition of the EOSat-1 spacecraft.
Primary and secondary structure made of aluminium honeycomb panels.
Deployable solar array wing with triple-junction GaAs cells.
Electrical power generated at end of life [W].
Li-ion battery pack powering the satellite during eclipses.
Reaction wheel for fine attitude control.
Star tracker providing absolute attitude knowledge.
Coarse sun sensor used in safe mode.
Magnetorquer used to dump the momentum of the reaction wheels.
On-board computer running the flight software.
S-band transceiver for telemetry and telecommand (TT&C).
X-band transmitter for payload data downlink.
Multispectral push-broom imager with a 5 m ground sampling distance.
Solid-state mass memory storing the payload images.
1 N hydrazine thruster for orbit maintenance.
Hydrazine propellant tank (dry mass, without propellant).
Physical architecture of the EOSat-1 spacecraft.
Electrical Power Subsystem (EPS): generates, stores and distributes power.
Communication Subsystem: TT&C in S-band and payload data downlink in X-band.
Payload: the imaging instrument and its data storage.
Propulsion Subsystem for orbit maintenance and end-of-life deorbiting.
